verdict: The HUD works as a debug-style stack of unrelated boxes. Nothing leads the eye, the type sizes are inconsistent, and the screen is cluttered with controls help and duplicate toasts.

findings.where: centre-bottom, controls legend (l stick / b / rt ...) at about 495-900 x 715-865
findings.what: A two-column key legend sits over the play area at about 14px, with a mono-looking tight list. It is dim on a translucent black box, with a mix of key names and actions and no grouping. It is pure clutter in a live raid. The tiny muted type fails couch readability, and the box has no accent or consistent padding. It also sits directly above 'in pillager's party' and the weapon prompt, so three overlays pile up.
findings.fix: Remove it from the raid HUD, or show it once and fade it after 5s. If kept, make it a P panel (#16191b at 90%, 1px #4a5257, 4px radius, 24px padding) with 16px labels in tx-1 and 16px actions in tx-2. Limit it to the 4 actions in use.

findings.what: Three bars use different treatments. 'standing' is a tab-like chip, stamina is a blue bar with a label in a different size, and hp is a solid green bar with oversized 'hp 100' text at about 32px. The text is crammed against the left edge of the bars with no padding, and the hp label is heavier than the hero ammo number's role. The block hugs the screen edge (about 24px from the left, 20px from the bottom) and ignores the 5% margin. The two bars are wide and flat with no frame, and there are no numeric values on stamina.
findings.fix: Use one bar component: 24px tall, 4px radius, #16191b track with a 1px border, a label at 16px f-cond 600 inside with 8px padding, and the value right-aligned. Reserve the single hero size (56px) for ammo. Inset the block to 5% margins (96px left, 54px bottom). Make the stance a small 16px tag above the bars.

findings.where: top-right career column ($900 / xp 0 / stash $0 / backpack $120)
findings.what: Four full-width bars of different heights (the first has no label at all), a 1px border and a dark fill. Values are right-aligned at about 20px, with labels in muted text, so it reads as a spreadsheet and not a HUD. The unlabelled $900 row and the xp row with 0 are noise. Spacing between rows is uneven (about 12px vs 16px), and the column is flush against the right edge with no margin. The minimap and run info stack directly below with a different panel treatment (the info panel has a chevron and uneven indents).
findings.fix: Keep this corner alone per the pending cw-trcol order, but make sure each row is a consistent 40px high with 8px gaps. Add a label to the first row, and drop xp when it is 0. Match the minimap and run info panels to the P spec (#16191b, 1px #4a5257, 4px radius, 24px padding) with a 16px label size.

findings.what: The contract lines wrap with inconsistent indentation ('extract with a haul worth / $1,200 or more 0/1'), and the text is cramped at about 16px with line spacing of about 4px. Mixed colours (teal/green 'no heals yet', white for the rest, muted for 'dawn clear') mean no clear hierarchy. The wrapped sentences read as explaining text, which is a listed defect. The header 'run info' has the same weight as the rows, and a stray chevron sits top-right with no obvious purpose.
findings.fix: Cut the text to short callouts such as 'haul $1,200  0/1', 'data core  0/1', 'cases  0/2'. Set the header at 16px tx-2, and the rows at 20px tx-1 with the 0/1 counters right-aligned in lime when active. Use 8px row gaps and 16px padding on all sides.

findings.where: top-left raid scoreboard 'current pillager bots 3' and the 'pillager' nameplate card
findings.what: The scoreboard header is amber at about 16px in the same box as the rows, so the box has no framing, and it competes with the extract timer for first-glance attention. The amber also violates the rule that warn amber is only a small glyph, because here it works as a header colour and is easy to confuse with the accent. The 'pillager' name card below it is a separate dark bar with a green line, a third panel style in one corner, floating with no alignment to the scoreboard. The left edges differ by a few px.
findings.fix: Make the scoreboard header tx-2 16px, with row text at 20px tx-1 and values right-aligned. Collapse it to the top 3 lines. Align the name card and the scoreboard to the same 96px left margin, and use the P panel spec on both.

findings.where: centre-top and mid-left toasts ('extract 146m' teal pill, 'controller connected' x2, 'keyboard' chip top-left, 'in pillager's party')
findings.what: The same 'controller connected' message shows twice, once top-centre and once bottom-left, and both stay on screen. 'keyboard' sits in the top-left corner in a lime-bordered chip that clips against the screen edge (about 8px). 'in pillager's party' and the weapon prompt 'scav pistol fire use' stack in the bottom centre with different box widths and fonts. The prompt's 'fire' key chip is tiny at about 14px. These are five different pill styles with different radii, fills and font sizes.
findings.fix: Show one toast at a time in a single toast component (#16191b, 1px #4a5257, 4px radius, 8px by 16px padding, 16px text) at a fixed slot under the timer. Drop the duplicate. Remove the 'keyboard' chip, since the device is already known from the key prompt, or move it inside the 5% margin. Turn the weapon prompt into a lime 16px key chip plus a tx-1 label.

findings.where: bottom-right weapon card and the hotbar
findings.what: The ammo card is the strongest element (the 12 / 24 hero), but the card is partly clipped at the screen edge and has a thin lime tab on its top-left, which is correct and the only place the accent works. The hotbar slots 3 to 0 are all dim silhouettes of near-identical weapons, so the row reads as eight empty tiles that eat a lot of width. The slot numbers are at about 12px, which is under the 14px floor. 'view backpack' at 20px sits left of the ammo and is lost in the card.
findings.fix: Dim empty slots to 40% and shrink them, or hide slots with no weapon. Raise slot numbers to 16px. Inset the ammo card to the 5% margin (48px right, 54px bottom) and put 'view backpack' as a 16px tx-2 hint under the weapon name instead of beside the hero number.

findings.what: The HUD is dark translucent boxes laid over a flat map with a warm-orange / blue-grey world palette, so panels get little contrast separation, and the HUD does not yet look like one family. Corner anchors differ (some boxes flush to the edge, some inset), the lime accent shows up in only one tab, and amber and teal take the highlight roles instead. It looks like a debug overlay and not an ARC Raiders-style flat panel with one hot accent.
findings.fix: Apply one panel component everywhere, with a 5% safe margin (96px x, 54px y). Reserve lime for focus, the active slot and the primary number only. Move amber to warnings only, and keep teal for extraction only.
